01 / THE SCENE

A miniature urban war.

Articulated low-poly infantry, tracked armor, and rotorcraft. Two fictional divisions advance through sixteen modular city blocks.

02 / THE DESTRUCTION

Damage with weight.

Shells and rockets break building sections free. Failed supports trigger cascading collapse. Debris tumbles, collides, and settles under gravity.

03 / THE LIMITS

A physics study.

Pre-segmented structures with simplified support rules, not engineering-grade concrete fracture. Active debris is capped for performance.

CROSSFIRE / AN OBSERVATIONAL EXPERIMENTTechnical notes ↗

Observe the battle.

The armies fight automatically. You control only the camera.

Phone: one finger to orbit, pinch to zoom, two fingers to pan. Arrow buttons raise/lower the camera. Turn your phone sideways for more space.

Desktop: drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom. WASD moves the camera; Q/E changes altitude. Shift moves faster.

Choose a camera preset to follow a tank, helicopter, or infantry soldier. Drag the view to return to free observation. Pause freezes combat and physics while the camera stays available.

Rebuild city restores the buildings and restarts the battle. Physics uses rigid building sections, simplified support checks, and a bounded active-debris budget.
